old_problem: The source provides only a project acronym and missing-spec placeholders. A generic scan cannot map responders to physical connectors, inventory EEPROMs, sensors, indicator drivers or controls. GPT V2's front-I/O model is plausible but not source-authorized, and neither review supplies the logical-to-physical oracle needed for coverage.
disposition_reason: Retain Pending and BLOCKED. Engineering must define FIO_BD's function, location, revision and populated physical resources before a safe controller path and response matrix can exist. Some endpoints can mix identity/status with button, LED or other control registers. Board identity, safe transaction semantics and any visual correlation are core requirements, not mere runtime bindings.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1807, same-row DeepSeek/test-json, GPT V2, historical record, pending/blocked analyses and ED-01 through ED-30 were read. The next formal locked-queue identity was directly opened as Functionality row 1808 / Wistron-HW-00010-V003 / fc6266db315d68a3.
FIO_BD defaults to BMC/platform-management scope, but project-specific acronym expansion and physical resource population cannot be guessed.
Address presence does not identify a connector/device or prove correct sensor/indicator state; physical LED evidence remains manual under ED-09 when required.
ED-03 forbids guessed OEM routes/registers and ED-15 forbids PASS without an approved per-resource response/state oracle.
Generic scanning can reach indicator, button, EEPROM or control endpoints and is not acceptable without a register-level allowlist.
No SSH, I2C, FIO, indicator, scan, write, reset, retry or DUT action was performed.

Stop on any FIO, indicator, sensor, BMC or bus anomaly; do not retry/reset automatically.

Controller/mux/bus/address/register allowlist, exclusions, tool/version and authenticated session
